title: Canonical biduality on bounded-above projective representatives
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathcal T$ be the category with one object $*$ and only its identity arrow, with only the maximal sieve covering, and let $\underline B$ be its ring sheaf with value $B$. Evaluation at $*$ and the inverse one-object sheaf construction give an exact equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B)\simeq B\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The induced equivalence of ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with localization universe equal to the coefficient universe, identifies product total sheaf Hom with the product total module Hom $H$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], carries K-injective complexes and their resolution augmentations to K-injective complexes and resolution augmentations, and identifies derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], coefficient evaluation, and its Koszul-symmetry bidual transpose. Write $Q$ for module localization, $O=B[0]$, $V^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(V,QO)$, and $b_V:V\to V^{\vee\vee}$ for that canonical transpose [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. If $T$ and $D=H(T,O)$ are both bounded above with projective terms [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], then for either $S=T,D$ the fixed K-injective augmentation $\eta_O:O\to I(O)$ induces a quasi-isomorphism $H(S,\eta_O)$ and the canonical comparison $\gamma_S:QH(S,O)\xrightarrow{\sim}(QS)^\vee$. For the signed chain map $\delta_T:T\to H(D,O)$ specified by $\delta_T(x)(\phi)=(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x)$ on homogeneous elements, with zero coordinates away from $|x|+|\phi|=0$, these comparisons satisfy $(\gamma_T)^\vee b_{QT}=\gamma_D Q(\delta_T)$. The comparisons are natural in chain maps and the derived bidual maps are natural on the whole derived category: $b_W e=e^{\vee\vee}b_V$ for every $e:V\to W$. No finite generation of the terms of $T$ or invertibility of $b_V$ is asserted.

Terminal-site Hom and resolution transport are the explicit specialization needed for the returned parent proof steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison] with $R=B$. It supplies the exact module equivalence, its constant-sheaf inverse, and the degreewise complex, homotopy and derived equivalences commuting with localization. Use these ordinary derived categories in the coefficient universe on both sides. It also supplies preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, K-flatness and tensor products. No geometric point or pro-etale point comparison is being substituted for this one-object site.

source.place: Tag 00X9, section-topoi, punctual topos; explicit one-object specialization.

proof.text: The slice $\mathcal T/*$ again has one object and only its identity. Thus [def-pur-sheaf-hom] evaluates to $\operatorname{Hom}_B(M(*),N(*))$, including its $B$-action. Products are sectionwise, so [def-pur-hom-complex] evaluates in degree $n$ to $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_B(L^p,M^{p+n})$; its differential is $d_Mf-(-1)^nfd_L$. This is exactly [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], with pre- and postcomposition unchanged. For K-injectivity use [def-pur-kinjective-complex]: a chain map from an acyclic complex and a null-homotopy are transported componentwise by the equivalence and its inverse. The equations $f=dh+hd$ remain the same, and acyclicity is preserved by step 1. Hence K-injectivity is preserved and reflected; an augmentation remains a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. In particular keep the image of the fixed augmentation, rather than choose a new map.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom; specialization to the punctual site.

proof.text: Compute derived internal Hom by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the transported K-injective resolutions from step 2. The resulting complexes on both sides are the same product Hom; [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] gives the canonical comparison if the module-side replacement is written using another K-injective model. This identifies the bifunctors after localization, including their maps. For evaluation retain the actual projections and the inverse localized augmentation of [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. For a K-flat representative with flat terms and a K-injective target, [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose] states that the derived tensor-Hom transpose of the existing closed structure is represented by the uncurrying rule $x\otimes y\mapsto\phi(x)(y)$, the normalization of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]; this holds on both sides, so their evaluations agree. The tensor and natural adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] identify their transposes; its Koszul symmetry is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on both sides. Consequently the coefficient-unit evaluation transpose is exactly the map $b$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. These identifications use the transported augmentations and normalized localization comparisons, not an arbitrary isomorphism of the derived Hom objects.

For either $S=T$ or $S=D$, bounded-above projective terms imply K-projectivity by [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective]. Put $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\eta_O)$. The augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, so $C$ is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. K-projectivity gives that $H(S,C)$ is acyclic. Apply [lem-sc-hom-complex-mapping-cone] on the one-object site and the identification of step 2 to obtain $\operatorname{Cone}(H(S,\eta_O))\cong H(S,C)$. A second application of [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] shows that $H(S,\eta_O)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This applies to the actual fixed augmentation, even when its target is unbounded.

source.place: Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective, proof using the map to a K-injective resolution.

proof.text: Write $\lambda_{S,O}:(QS)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}QH(S,I(O))$ for the fixed resolution factorization. By [def-trf-ringed-hom-representative-comparison] the comparison is the actual composite $\gamma_S=\lambda_{S,O}^{-1}\circ Q(H(S,\eta_O))$. Step 4 makes it invertible. For a chain map $f:S\to S'$ between such representatives, postcomposition with $\eta_O$ commutes with precomposition by $f$: both composites send $h$ to $\eta_O\circ h\circ f$. The localization factorization in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is natural. Therefore $\gamma_S\circ QH(f,O)=(Qf)^\vee\circ\gamma_{S'}$. This proves naturality of the specified comparisons without assuming finite generation.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom; specialization to the punctual site.

proof.text: Apply the bidual representative normalization of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] to $E=T$ on the one-object site. Its two hypotheses are precisely the quasi-isomorphisms of step 4 for $T$ and $D$. Its signed chain map evaluates to $(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x)$; every coordinate with $|x|+|\phi|\ne0$ lands in a zero term of $O$. Thus it is the specified $\delta_T$ under step 2. The fixed comparisons in that normalization are the $\gamma_T,\gamma_D$ of step 5. Written with their codomains displayed, the normalization says $H(\gamma_T,QO)\circ b_{QT}=\gamma_D\circ Q(\delta_T)$, which is the required equation. The same cited node states covariance of $b$ on all derived objects, so $b_W\circ e=e^{\vee\vee}\circ b_V$ for every derived morphism $e:V\to W$. Neither this normalization nor its naturality assumes invertibility of $b$, and step 4 used projectivity without finite generation.
